premise.claim: With rbg.workloads.x-k8s.io/group-exclusive-topology: kubernetes.io/hostname on a v1alpha2 RoleBasedGroup, the group's first Pod never schedules, even when free untainted nodes exist: '0/4 nodes are available: 2 node(s) didn't match pod affinity rules, 2 node(s) had untolerated taint(s).'
premise.reportedComponent: pkg/reconciler/pod_reconciler.go (ConstructPodTemplateSpecApplyConfiguration -> setExclusiveAffinities), v1alpha2 default RoleInstanceSet path
premise.evidence: L1+L2 harness grafted onto base 1fc69f70: injected required podAffinity selects group-unique-hash while Pod labels carry group-uid; nothing on base sets group-unique-hash (git grep at base). results/L1-base-premise.log, results/L2-base-premise.log

integration.cmd: KUBEBUILDER_ASSETS=$(ls -d /home/ecs-user/.local/share/kubebuilder-envtest/k8s/1.31.0-linux-amd64 2>/dev/null || echo bin/k8s/1.31.0-linux-amd64) go test ./test/envtest/testcase/rbg/ -count=1 -timeout=8m -ginkgo.focus 'reviewer verify'

match: injects group-uid affinity that matches the Pod's own labels, and toggles with the annotation

liveNote: L3 (real scheduler on a real cluster) is out of scope for this round. Observable signal to check when run: the first Pod of a fresh exclusive group leaves Pending (FailedScheduling stops), same-group Pods co-locate, and another group pinned to that node stays Pending with an anti-affinity FailedScheduling event. The PR's own e2e (test/e2e/testcase/v1alpha2/rbg.go, ginkgo 'lifecycle' label) asserts all of these and runs in the CI lifecycle matrix.
